name: tag_update

path.udtDefinitionNamespace: only under an explicit _types_ allowlist entry

nativeOutcome: one system.tag.configure call per item; its single QualityCode is that item's outcome, and Observed state never decides success

preconditionToken.comparedRead: system.tag.exists(path) and then system.tag.getConfiguration(path, false, false) for every item, before any item executes
preconditionToken.raceWindow: D30 2: the compare and the change are two steps, so a competing writer can change or delete a target between the Preflight read and system.tag.configure. The handler narrows what it can (every fingerprint is read before any dispatch, and a target the Preflight read found missing is refused with not_found) and claims no atomicity. A target that disappears inside the window is re-created by MergeOverwrite, which is the same race the D16 final-import window documents; a caller that needs a narrower window re-reads with tag_get_config and retries the whole batch.

preflight: input, reserved provider and Target allowlist for every item before any item executes, with no rollback

runtimeTargetPolicy.allowlistMatch: provider-qualified config path prefix at segment boundaries; explicit * allows every provider but never a UDT definition
runtimeTargetPolicy.reservedProviderRefusal: permission_denied before Preflight, whatever the allowlist says, including an explicit *

targetPath.form: <provider>Tag, <provider>Folder or <provider>Folder/Tag, and <provider>_types_/... for a UDT definition
targetPath.noWildcard: a config target is one exact path: a *, ? or : anywhere in it is invalid_argument
targetPath.leaf: the target's last segment is the definition name sent to system.tag.configure

udtDefinitionTargets: an explicit _types_ allowlist entry only: a target whose first post-provider segment is _types_ (D30 6's [provider]_types_/...) is refused with permission_denied unless a matching entry whose own first post-provider segment is _types_ covers it, so a bare * does not cover a UDT definition, while a folder that is merely called _types_ deeper in the path stays an ordinary target (D30 6)
creatingMissingTargets: Preflight reads every target's configuration and refuses the whole batch with not_found when a target is not there, so the handler never creates one

refusedConfigKeys.value: invalid_argument (configValueIsAControlWrite): a Tag value write is tag_write's, and this Tool belongs to the CONFIG class
refusedConfigKeys.tags: invalid_argument (configNestedTagsNotAllowed): a child is its own target with its own fingerprint, so it is updated as its own item
refusedConfigKeys.name: invalid_argument (configNameChangeNotAllowed): a name change is tag_rename's, which checks the new path against the Target allowlist

ambiguousOutcomeScope: an item whose own dispatch raised is outcome_unknown and ends the batch (later items are not_executed); an item whose dispatch answered an unattributable QualityCode is outcome_unknown and the batch continues. Nothing is replayed

existenceCheck.call: system.tag.exists(path) for every item, before that item's fingerprint is read and before any item executes
existenceCheck.why: a Gateway answers system.tag.getConfiguration for a path that is not there with a synthesized default node, so the configuration read alone cannot tell the caller whether the target exists; the ticket #10 live run recorded the same synthesized node on 8.3.8 and 8.3.9
existenceCheck.missing: not_found (details.items[].reason = targetMissing), and nothing is dispatched
existenceCheck.unanswered: upstream_error (reasons existenceCheckFailed / existenceCheckIndeterminate): a Gateway that raises or answers something that is not a boolean is never read as present
existenceCheck.observedReadBacks: the provider export is the independent absence check the harness uses

inputBounds.hardItemsPolicyRule: a deployment may raise the 20-target default through the Runtime Target Policy and never above the 100-target hard ceiling

deniedMutationAudit: after a usable Policy is read, a refused Target and a refused Precondition each produce one `decision` row and no dispatch; `off` records nothing, and `required` refuses the call when the denial row cannot be written
outcomePreservation: a dispatched batch reports its per-item Native outcomes whatever the Observed-state budget or the serializer does; an Observed configuration that cannot be returned is an explicit `limit_exceeded` observed error, and the result is re-rendered without the Observed state rather than replacing the outcomes
